issue.title: Python wheel for RPI
issue.body:
I am currently trying to run MAVSDK within Docker containers on RPi 4.
I have it working outside of Docker by building it using the guidelines in this post:
https://discuss.px4.io/t/talking-to-a-px4-fmu-with-a-rpi-via-serial-nousb-ardunope/14119
I am doing this because pip install mavsdk is not supported for the RPi at this time.

The post does mention that there is some interest in creating a python wheel for RPi.
As this does not yet exist I am currently looking into creating a base Docker image that contains an already built version of MavSDK-python and python3. Hopefully this way I don't need to built mavSDK every time I want to build a Docker Image with MAVsdk included.

Are there any plans for supporting/enabling pip install mavsdk on RPi?
And even if supported/enabled, would it no longer require the long built times?

Until then, when I get my base Image for python 3 + mavSDK-python working, I will comment my findings in this issue.

(This is my first GitHub issue ever, please let me know if I am not following styling guidelines, formatting or other conventions,...)

comments.body:
> pip install mavsdk on RPi?

The problem is that Linux builds on PyPi are built using `manylinux1` or `manylinux2010`. They are `x86_64` based and therefore don't include `arm` binaries. This might change with `manylinux2014`, check https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK-Python/issues/117.

What we could/should do alternatively, is provide a RPi .deb package to install the `mavsdk_server` binary which is all that is needed for the RPi platform. You could then use that within docker or directly.

I don't have any experience with these .deb packages.
I did manage to create a Docker container based on a standard Python container and install mavsdk into it. I've placed this as an image on docker hub under the name mavsdk-python-armv8 in a private repository as well. I don't want to confuse people into using it for any kind of critical application, that's why its private for now. I could make it public with a clear description, just let me know.

I am however convinced that the .deb solution would be better, my current Docker image is 3GB in uncompressed size...
Would it be feasible for  me to create this with some research (again, no experience with .deb)? Or is this coming in the near future anyway?

For now i will leave my Dockerfile here:
```
FROM python:3

# Set the working directory, this is the image file system
WORKDIR /usr/src/app

RUN apt update
RUN apt upgrade

RUN apt-get update -y
RUN apt-get install cmake build-essential colordiff git doxygen -y 

RUN git clone https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK.git
WORKDIR /usr/src/app/MAVSDK
RUN git checkout master
RUN git submodule update --init --recursive
RUN cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=ON -Bbuild/default -H.
RUN cmake --build build/default
RUN cmake --build build/default --target install
RUN ldconfig

# Building the mavsdk-server
RUN cmake -DBUILD_BACKEND=ON --symlink-install --cmake-args "-DCMAKE_SHARED_LINKER_FLAGS='-latomic'" "-DCMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS='-latomic'" -Bbuild/default -H.
RUN cmake --build build/default

WORKDIR /usr/src/app/
RUN git clone https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK-Python --recursive
WORKDIR /usr/src/app/MAVSDK-Python/proto/pb_plugins
RUN pip3 install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt
# Needs to be the -e (editable) version or doesn't work, don't know why though
RUN pip3 install --no-cache-dir -e .

WORKDIR /usr/src/app/MAVSDK-Python
RUN pip3 install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt -r requirements-dev.txt
RUN ./other/tools/run_protoc.sh
# Needs to be the -e (editable) version or doesn't work, don't know why though
RUN pip3 install --no-cache-dir -e .
RUN mv /usr/src/app/MAVSDK/build/default/src/backend/src/mavsdk_server /usr/src/app/MAVSDK-Python/mavsdk/bin/

# removing built tools
RUN pip3 uninstall -r requirements-dev.txt -y
RUN apt-get --purge remove cmake build-essential colordiff git doxygen -y
RUN apt autoremove -y
# removing some files from MAVSDK to save some storage space.
WORKDIR /usr/src/app/
RUN rm -r ./MAVSDK/example ./MAVSDK/tools ./MAVSDK/.git ./MAVSDK-Python/examples ./MAVSDK-Python/tests

# build the image using: docker image build -t mavsdk-python-armv8:0.1 .
# run the image using: docker run --rm -it -p 127.0.0.1:4001:14540/udp 62imageid4551 sh

# To test the docker container, you can copy the telemetry.py file into a running container.
```

The 127.0.0.1:4001 is simply the port i chose to route my mavlink messages to on the host.

Nice, thanks for documenting all you did, that can certainly be helpful.

Regarding .deb files. We already have that for x86_64, if you look at the release assets: https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/releases/tag/v0.24.0

The current debs are however without the mavsdk_server but only the library. I think a first step is to extend the debs to include the mavsdk_server and then in a second step build it as part of the dockcross arm builds.
This now works using statically compiled mavsdk_server binaries using musl.

issue.title: issue with MAVSDK-Python version 0.5.2
issue.body:
Hi,

I'm trying to run MAVSDK-Python on an embedded system. So far I have been using the Odroid XU4 board and the Jetson Nano.
When I follow the standard procedure for installing the package (pip3 install mavsdk), it strikes me as quite odd that the version that it is automatically installed in both boards is the 0.5.2. Whereas if I do the same in my PC, the version that is installed is the 0.4.0. With the latter I have no issue whatsoever, but I can't install that one on any of the boards.

If I install the version 0.5.2 in my PC I get the same error as in the boards, which is the following:

```File "/home/odroid/Documents/git/px4-mission-code/src/DSI/Drone.py", line 471, in _connect
    await self.system.connect(system_address="udp://:14540")
  File "/home/odroid/.local/lib/python3.6/site-packages/mavsdk/system.py", line 62, in connect
    self._start_mavsdk_server(system_address)
  File "/home/odroid/.local/lib/python3.6/site-packages/mavsdk/system.py", line 172, in _start_mavsdk_server
    stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
  File "/usr/lib/python3.6/subprocess.py", line 729, in __init__
    restore_signals, start_new_session)
  File "/usr/lib/python3.6/subprocess.py", line 1364, in _execute_child
    raise child_exception_type(errno_num, err_msg, err_filename)
PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/home/odroid/.local/lib/python3.6/site-packages/mavsdk/bin/mavsdk_server'
```

All systems are running Ubuntu 18.04.

I have first tried to give the mavsdk_server file the execution permissions, as per default it did not have them, with no success either.
And I have also tried to build both the mavsdk server and the Mavsdk-Python from source, again no success there.

I would appreciate very much if you could help me solve this issue.
Thank you in advance.

issue.title: Run MAVSDK-Python on a Jetson Nano
issue.body:
When I ran TakeoffAndLand.py I was also getting the message telling me to manually build mavsdk myself. Because I installed it using pip3. So I built it according to the directions in the C++ section of mavsdk.
Couple questions 
1. when i run ./mavsdk_server where do I do it? I've tried to run it from linux home and inside the mavsdk folder and it doesnt exist
2.  Also im using a jetson nano to connect to a pixhawk through USB so the endpoint should be /dev/ttyUSB0:57600? So dronekit python will tell mavsdk_server to go look for a pixhawk connected through usb?
Thanks
